{{Short description|Criterion for convergence of continued fractions}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Śleszyński–Pringsheim theorem''' is a statement about [[Convergent (continued fraction)|convergence]] of certain [[continued fraction]]s. It was discovered by [[Ivan Śleszyński]]<ref>{{cite journal|last=Слешинскій|first=И. В.|title=Дополненiе къ замѣткѣ о сходимости непрерывныхъ дробей|journal=Матем. Сб.|volume=14|issue=3|year=1889|pages=436&ndash;438|url=http://mi.mathnet.ru/msb7210|language=Russian}}</ref> and [[Alfred Pringsheim]]<ref>{{cite journal|jfm=29.0178.02|last=Pringsheim|first=A.|title=Ueber die Convergenz unendlicher Kettenbrüche|language=German|journal=Münch. Ber.|volume=28|pages=295&ndash;324|year=1898}}</ref> in the late 19th century.<ref>W. J. Thron has found evidence that Pringsheim was aware of the work of Śleszyński before he published his article; see {{cite journal|mr=1192192|last=Thron|first=W. J.|title=Should the Pringsheim criterion be renamed the Śleszyński criterion?|journal=Comm. Anal. Theory Contin. Fractions|volume=1|year=1992|pages=13&ndash;20}}</ref>

It states that if <math>n</math> is a positive [[integer]] and <math>(a_n)</math>, <math>(b_n)</math> are [[sequence]]s of [[real number]]s such that <math>|b_n| \geq |a_n| + 1</math> for all <math>n</math>, then

<math display="block">\cfrac{a_1}{b_1 + \cfrac{a_2}{b_2 + \cfrac{a_3}{b_3 + \ddots}}}</math>

converges absolutely to a number <math>x</math> satisfying <math>|x| \leq 1</math>,<ref>{{cite book|first1=L.|last1=Lorentzen|first2=H.|last2=Waadeland|title=Continued Fractions: Convergence theory|publisher=Atlantic Press|year=2008|page=129}}</ref> meaning that the series

<math display="block">x = \sum_n \left\{ \frac{A_n}{B_n} - \frac{A_{n - 1}}{B_{n - 1}} \right\},</math>

where <math>A_n / B_n</math> are the [[convergent (continued fraction)|convergents]] of the continued fraction, [[absolute convergence|converges absolutely]].

== Proof ==
Recall that the <math>n</math>th convergents of <math>x</math>, which will be denoted by <math>\tfrac{A_n}{B_n}</math> in this article, can be computed from the following [[recurrence relation]]:

<math display="block">\begin{align}
A_n &:= b_n A_{n - 1} + a_n A_{n - 2} \\
B_n &:= b_n B_{n - 1} + a_n B_{n - 2}, \qquad n \geq 2
\end{align}</math>

where <math>A_0 = 0</math>, <math>A_1 = a_1</math>, <math>B_0 = 1</math>, and <math>B_1 = b_1</math>. See [[Continued fraction#Formulation|this article]] for more detail.

=== {{mvar|n}}th convergent as a series ===

First, we will prove the following claim via [[mathematical induction]]

{{Math theorem
| name = Claim
| math_statement =
For all positive integers <math>n</math>, then
<math display="block">A_n B_{n - 1} - A_{n - 1} B_n = (-1)^{n - 1} a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n</math>}}

{{Math proof
| proof =
The case <math>n = 1</math> is trivial.

Suppose the claim is true for <math>n = k</math>. By using the two recurrence relation above, it follows that

<math display="block">\begin{align}
A_{k + 1} B_k - A_k B_{k + 1} &= \left( b_{k + 1} A_k + a_{k + 1} A_{k - 1} \right) B_k - A_k \left( b_{k + 1} B_k + a_{k + 1} B_{k - 1} \right) \\
&= b_{k + 1} A_k B_k + a_{k + 1} A_{k - 1} B_k - b_{k + 1} A_k B_k - a_{k + 1} A_k B_{k - 1} \\
&= a_{k + 1} A_{k - 1} B_k - a_{k + 1} A_k B_{k - 1} \\
&= - a_{k + 1} \left( A_k B_{k - 1} - A_{k - 1} B_k \right) \\
&= - a_{k + 1} \cdot (-1)^{k - 1} a_1 a_2 \cdots a_k \\
&= (-1)^k a_1 a_2 \cdots a_k a_{k + 1}
\end{align}</math>

which finishes the induction step.}}

By dividing [[sides of an equation|both sides]] of the claim by <math>B_n \cdot B_{n - 1}</math>, the equation becomes

<math display="block">\dfrac{A_n}{B_n} - \dfrac{A_{n - 1}}{B_{n - 1}} = (-1)^{n - 1} \dfrac{a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n}{B_{n - 1} \cdot B_n}</math>

Thus,

<math display="block">\begin{align}
\sum_{i \, = \, 1}^{n} \dfrac{A_i}{B_i} - \dfrac{A_{i - 1}}{B_{i - 1}} &= \sum_{i \, = \, 1}^{n} (-1)^{i - 1} \dfrac{a_1 a_2 \cdots a_i}{B_{i - 1} B_i} \\
\dfrac{A_n}{B_n} - \dfrac{A_0}{B_0} &= \dfrac{a_1}{B_0 B_1} - \dfrac{a_1 a_2}{B_1 B_2} + \dfrac{a_1 a_2 a_3}{B_2 B_3} - \ldots + (-1)^{n - 1} \dfrac{a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n}{B_{n - 1} B_n} \\
\dfrac{A_n}{B_n} &= \dfrac{a_1}{B_0 B_1} - \dfrac{a_1 a_2}{B_1 B_2} + \dfrac{a_1 a_2 a_3}{B_2 B_3} - \ldots + (-1)^{n - 1} \dfrac{a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n}{B_{n - 1} B_n}
\end{align}</math>

=== Absolute value of {{mvar|n}}th convergent as a series ===

Now suppose that <math>|b_n| \geq |a_n| + 1</math> for all <math>n</math>. Using the recurrence relation of <math>(B_n)</math>, note that

<math display="block">\left| b_n B_{n - 1} \right| = \left| B_n - a_n B_{n - 2} \right| \leq \left| B_n \right| + \left| a_n B_{n - 2} \right|.</math>

Thus,

<math display="block">\begin{align}
\left| B_n \right| &\geq \left| b_n \right| \left| B_{n - 1} \right| - \left| a_n \right| \left| B_{n - 2} \right| \\
&\geq \left( \left| a_n \right| + 1 \right) \left| B_{n - 1} \right| - \left| a_n \right| \left| B_{n - 2} \right| \\
\left| B_n \right| - \left| B_{n - 1} \right| &\geq \left| a_n \right| \left( \left| B_{n - 1} \right| - \left| B_{n - 2} \right| \right) 
\end{align}</math>

Since <math>\left| B_1 \right| - \left| B_0 \right| = \left| b_1 \right| - 1 \geq \left| a_1 \right|</math> by assumption, then by using mathematical induction, one can show that

<math display="block>\left| B_n \right| - \left| B_{n - 1} \right| \geq \prod_{i \, = \, 1}^{n} \left| a_i \right|.</math>

Consequently, the sequence of <math>\left| B_n \right|</math> is [[Monotonic function|monotone nondecreasing]] and [[Bounded function|bounded from below]] by <math>\left| B_0 \right| = 1</math>. Moreover, 

<math display="block">\dfrac{1}{\left| B_n B_{n - 1} \right|} \prod_{i \, = \, 1}^{n} \left| a_i \right| \leq \dfrac{\left| B_n \right| - \left| B_{n - 1} \right|}{\left| B_n B_{n - 1} \right|} = \dfrac{1}{\left| B_{n - 1} \right|} - \dfrac{1}{\left| B_n \right|}</math>

Since the right-hand side forms a [[telescoping series]], it is easy to see that

<math display="block">\dfrac{\left| a_1 \right|}{\left| B_0 B_1 \right|} + \dfrac{\left| a_1 a_2 \right|}{\left| B_1 B_2 \right|} + \ldots + \dfrac{\left| a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n \right|}{\left| B_{n - 1} B_n \right|} \leq \dfrac{1}{\left| B_0 \right|} - \dfrac{1}{\left| B_n \right|} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{\left| B_n \right|} < 1</math>

for all values of <math>n</math>. Furthermore, the nondecreasing property of the sequence <math>\left| B_n \right|</math> also implies the nondecreasing property of the sequence <math>1 - \tfrac{1}{\left| B_n \right|}</math>. Thus, the sequence <math>1 - \tfrac{1}{\left| B_n \right|}</math> must converge, by the [[monotone convergence theorem]].

Note that the left-hand side is the upper bound of series representation of <math>\left| \tfrac{A_n}{B_n} \right|</math> after applying [[triangle inequality]], which completes the proof.
